name: Roomote

hlido_opinion.headline: A cloud coding agent that takes ownership seriously — self-hostable, single-tenant, model-agnostic BYOK, and it runs your actual app before claiming the work is done.
hlido_opinion.body: Roomote, from the team behind Roo Code, is a cloud coding agent built around a specific objection: most hosted agents ask you to give up control of the environment, the model, and the tenancy. Roomote answers each one. It is self-hostable or run on their cloud, always single-tenant, model-agnostic with bring-your-own-key, source-available, and works across GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Gitea and Bitbucket rather than assuming GitHub. For teams whose blocker to adopting an agent is procurement rather than capability, that list is the pitch. The execution loop is the second substantive part. Roomote runs your real dev environment, verifies its own work, reviews the change with a *different* model than the one that wrote it, and returns a pull request with a live preview URL for reviewers to inspect. Cross-model review is a meaningful design choice — self-review by the authoring model is the known weak point in agentic coding — and a live running app beats a diff for catching what a diff cannot show. Interaction happens where teams already are: Slack, Teams, Discord, Telegram, plus a mobile web UI, which makes the async framing credible rather than aspirational. What the surface does not settle: there are no named customers or case studies, "source available" is not the same as open source and the licence terms are not stated on the landing page, and the built-in analytics and automation claims are described but not evidenced. Pricing is a nav item, so terms exist, but the reviewed capture did not resolve them.

tier_rationale: STEADY (78) for a coherent, control-preserving architecture — self-hostable, single-tenant, BYOK, multi-forge — combined with an execution loop that verifies against a running application and reviews with a second model. Those are substantive engineering choices, not marketing. Not VITAL because the surface carries no named customers or case studies, the licence behind 'source available' is unstated, and the automation and analytics claims are asserted without evidence a buyer can check.
what_it_does_well: Self-hostable or cloud, always single-tenant — answers the real procurement objection
Model-agnostic with BYOK; no lock-in to a single provider's pricing or capability
Reviews its own changes with a different model than the one that wrote them
Runs the actual application and hands reviewers a live preview URL, not just a diff
Works across GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Gitea and Bitbucket
Operates through Slack, Teams, Discord and Telegram, making async use credible
Built by the Roo Code team — an existing track record in the category
what_it_fails_at: No named customers or case studies on the surface
'Source available' stated without naming the licence — not equivalent to open source
Automation and built-in analytics claims are described but not evidenced
Pricing exists as a nav item but terms are not resolved on the landing surface
Self-hosting cost and operational burden are not discussed
'Unlimited parallel tasks' is asserted without stating what bounds it in practice
best_for: Teams whose blocker is tenancy, data residency or model choice rather than agent capability
Organisations on GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea or Azure DevOps that most agents ignore
Async and mobile-heavy workflows driven from chat tools
Reviewers who want to click a running app rather than read a diff
not_recommended_for: Solo developers wanting the simplest possible local setup
Buyers who need a named licence before adopting source-available software
Teams requiring published customer references for procurement

compared_to.verdict_diff: Cursor is a local editor-based agent; Roomote is cloud/self-hosted and PR-oriented with live previews. Cursor for interactive in-editor work, Roomote for async delegated tasks that come back as reviewable pull requests.

Aider is a fully open local CLI with no infrastructure; Roomote adds hosted or self-hosted execution, cross-model review and live previews at the cost of running something. Aider for minimalism, Roomote for team workflow.

Windsurf is an agentic IDE with a polished local experience; Roomote gives up the editor to gain single-tenancy, BYOK and multi-forge support. Windsurf for editor experience, Roomote for control and deployment flexibility.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Roomote is itself an autonomous coding agent rather than a component agents call. It integrates inbound through git forges (issues, PRs) and chat platforms, which gives an event-driven path for triggering work, and self-hosting means the deployment is scriptable. No public API, MCP server or SDK is documented for driving Roomote programmatically.
